en: An overseer of congregations: either any such overseer, generally speaking, or (in Eastern Orthodoxy, Catholicism, Anglicanism, etc.) an …
A chief of the Festival of Fools or St. Nicholas Day.
To act as a bishop, to perform the duties of a bishop, especially to confirm another's membership in the church.
To make a bishop.

bishop.ety:
From Middle English bischop, bishop, bisshop, biscop, from Old English bisċop (“bishop”), from Proto-West Germanic *biskop, from Vulgar Latin (e)biscopus, from classical Latin episcopus (“overseer, supervisor”), from Ancient Greek ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos, “overseer”), from ἐπί (epí, “over”) + σκοπός (skopós, “watcher”), used in Greek and Latin both generally and as a title of civil officers. Cognate with all European terms for the position in various Christian churches; compare also Middle English bisp (“bishop”).
* The Tyndale Bible uses native English overseer instead.

ex.en: The bishops were in favor of the proposition.
ex.ja: 司教達はその提案に賛成であった。

ex.en: The bishop took pity on the desperate immigrants.
ex.ja: 宗教は、自暴自棄になった移民達を哀れんで助けを与えた。

ex.en: The bishop felt pity for the immigrants who were abandoned, and gave them help.
ex.ja: 司教は、自暴自棄になった移民たちを哀れんで助けを与えた。

en: As a rule; frequently; usually.

commonly.ety: Inherited from Middle English comunly; equivalent to common + -ly.

ex.en: Women commonly live longer than men.
ex.ja: 女性は通常男性よりも長生きする。

ex.en: This sentence is commonly used.
ex.ja: この文はよく使われるよ。

ex.en: Antibiotics are commonly enzymatic inhibitors.
ex.ja: 抗生物質は一般的に酵素の阻害剤である。

en: Intended for defence; protective.
Intended to deter attack.
A means, attitude or position of defense. Chiefly in on the defensive.

defensive.ety: From Middle French défensif. Morphologically defense + -ive.

ex.en: Defensive driving can help you avoid accidents.
ex.ja: 予防運転は事故を防ぎます。

en: The extent to which a resource is used for the intended purpose.
The ratio of useful work to energy expended. Often given the symbol η.

efficiency.ety: From Latin efficientia, equivalent to efficient + -cy.

ex.en: He put forward a plan for improving office efficiency.
ex.ja: 彼は事務効率をよくする案を出した。

ex.en: Efficiency is the dominant idea in business.
ex.ja: 商売では能率のよさということが最も重要な考えである。

ex.en: That makes for efficiency.
ex.ja: そうすれば能率が上がりますよ。

en: A company, business, organization, or other purposeful endeavor.
An undertaking, venture, or project, especially a daring and courageous one.
To undertake an enterprise, or something hazardous or difficult.
To undertake; to begin and attempt to perform; to venture upon.

enterprise.ety: From Old French via Middle English and Middle French entreprise, feminine past participle of entreprendre (“to undertake”), from entre (“in between”) + prendre (“to take”), from Latin inter + prehendō, see prehensile.

ex.en: He played an important part in the enterprise.
ex.ja: 彼はその事業において重要な役割を演じた。

ex.en: Building the steel factory was a great enterprise.
ex.ja: その製鉄工場を建てるのは非常に大変な事業だった。

ex.en: Commercial Code can be called an enterprise method.
ex.ja: 商法は企業法といえる。

note.ja: enter（= inter 間に）+ pris（取る）+ e。手中に取ること →（困難なことに着手する）→「企業・事業・冒険心」。

en: A test under controlled conditions made to either demonstrate a known truth, examine the validity of a hypothesis, or determine the effic…
To conduct an experiment.
To try something to observe the results.

experiment.ety: From Middle English experiment, from Old French esperiment (French expérience), from Latin experimentum (“experience, attempt, experiment”), from experior (“to experience, to attempt”), itself from ex + *perior, in turn from Proto-Indo-European *per-.

ex.en: We used the following procedures in this experiment.
ex.ja: この実験には以下の手段を使用した。

ex.en: They carried out a new experiment in chemistry.
ex.ja: 彼らは化学の新しい実験をした。

ex.en: We were disappointed with the results of the experiment.
ex.ja: 私達は実験の結果にがっかりした。

en: A place for discussion.
A gathering for the purpose of discussion; a symposium.

forum.ety: From Latin forum (“public market place, forum”). Doublet of fuero and door.

ex.en: I moved the forum to a new server.
ex.ja: 掲示板を新しいサーバーに移転しました。

ex.en: The forum was moved to a new server.
ex.ja: 掲示板を新しいサーバーに移転しました。

ex.en: I do not have an account in these forums.
ex.ja: これらのフォームのアカウントを私はもってません。

en: Any plant of the family Poaceae, characterized by leaves that arise from nodes in the stem and leaf bases that wrap around the stem, espe…
Any of the various plants that are not in the family Poaceae that resemble grasses.
To lay out on the grass; to knock down (an opponent etc.).
To cover with grass or with turf.

grass.ety:

Proto-West Germanic *gras

Cognates
Cognate with Scots gress (“grass”), North Frisian gaars, geers, Gērs, gjars, gjas, gäärs (“grass”), Saterland Frisian Gäärs (“grass”), West Frisian gers (“grass”), Cimbrian gras, grass (“grass”), German and Luxembourgish Gras (“grass, weed”), Dutch gras (“grass, turf,

ex.en: He made do with a bed of grass.
ex.ja: 彼はベッドを草で間に合わせた。

ex.en: He lay at full length on the grass.
ex.ja: 彼はその芝生に大の字になって寝そべった。

ex.en: This grass is too wet to sit on.
ex.ja: この芝生は座れないほどぬれている。

en: In the future from now.
As a result; therefore, for this reason.

hence.ety:
A later Middle English spelling, retaining the voiceless -s, of hennes (henne + adverbial genitive ending -s), from Old English heonan (“away", "hence”), from a Proto-West Germanic *hin-, from Proto-Germanic *hiz, and Proto-Germanic *-anē.
Cognate with Old Saxon hinan, Old High German hinnan (German hinnen), Dutch heen, Swedish hän. Related to Old English her (“here”).

ex.en: Hence, I shall have to stay here.
ex.ja: それゆえここにとどまらざるを得ないだろう。

ex.en: What will become of the world thirty years hence?
ex.ja: 今から３０年後に世界はどうなるだろう？

ex.en: It will be all the same a hundred years hence.
ex.ja: 百年後にはみな同じになる。

en: Increasing in amount or intensity.

increasingly.ety: From Middle English encreessingli, equivalent to increasing + -ly.

ex.en: Modern finance is becoming increasingly complicated and sophisticated.
ex.ja: 現代の金融は一段と複雑かつ高度になってきている。

ex.en: In recent years electronic computers have become increasingly important.
ex.ja: 近年では、電子コンピューターがますます重要になってきた。

ex.en: The world's aviation industry is growing increasingly worried about crashes.
ex.ja: 世界の航空産業は墜落事故についての懸念を募らせている。

en: In an incredible manner; not to be believed.
To a great extent; extremely.

incredibly.ety:
Etymology tree
English incredible
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English incredibly
From incredible + -ly.

ex.en: Tom is incredibly bad at drawing.
ex.ja: トムはびっくりするくらいに絵が下手だ。

ex.en: This summer is incredibly hot.
ex.ja: 今年の夏は異常に暑い。

ex.en: George has an incredibly large Adam's apple.
ex.ja: ジョージののどぼとけは信じられないぐらい大きい。

zh: 新聞工作者 /新闻工作者

en: The keeper of a personal journal, who writes in it regularly.
One whose occupation is journalism, originally only writing in the printed press.

Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti

ex.en: The journalist was calm even in an emergency.
ex.ja: その記者は緊急事態のときでも落ち着いていた。

ex.en: I thought of the woman as a journalist.
ex.ja: 私はその女性を記者だと思っていた。

ex.en: I've made up my mind to become a journalist.
ex.ja: 私はジャーナリストになる決心をしました。

The building housing such a grinding apparatus; also, any similar building that houses a similarly material activity (such as weaving, fu…
To grind or otherwise process in a mill or other machine.
To shape, polish, dress or finish using a machine.

From Middle English mylne, mille, from Old English mylen, from Proto-West Germanic *mulīnu (“mill”), from Late Latin molīna, molīnum, molīnus (“mill”), from Latin molō (“grind, mill”, verb), closely allied to Proto-Germanic *muljaną (“to crush, grind”) (see English mills

ex.en: There is a water mill above the bridge.
ex.ja: この橋の上流に水車小屋がある。

ex.en: The coffee mill that I received does not work.
ex.ja: 受け取ったコーヒーミルが動きません。

ex.en: Every miller draws water to his own mill.
ex.ja: 水車小屋は皆自分の水車に水を引く。

en: A favorable opportunity; a convenient or timely chance.
The time when something happens.
To cause; to produce; to induce

occasion.ety: From Middle English occasioun, from Middle French occasion, from Old French occasiun, from Latin occāsiōnem, noun of action from perfect passive participle occāsus, from verb occidō, from prefix ob- (“down", "away”) + verb cadō (“fall”).

ex.en: He offered his congratulations on the happy occasion.
ex.ja: そのめでたいときに当たり彼は祝辞を述べた。

ex.en: We meet him on occasion at the club.
ex.ja: 私たちは時折クラブで彼に出会います。

ex.en: I meet her on occasion at the club.
ex.ja: 私は彼女にときおりクラブで会います。

note.ja: oc（〜に向かって）+ cas（落ちる）+ ion。降りかかってくる時 →「場合・機会・行事」。

en: A step taken with the foot.
The distance covered in a step (or sometimes two), either vaguely or according to various specific set measurements.
Describing a bowler who bowls fast balls.
To walk back and forth in a small distance.
To walk along or through sth with regular strides.
With all due respect to.

pace.ety: From Middle English pase, from Anglo-Norman pas, Old French pas, and their source, Latin passus. Doublet of pas and fathom; compare also pass. Cognate with pass, Spanish pasear, paso.

ex.en: I want to live at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースに生きたい。

ex.en: I want to work at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースで仕事したい。

ex.en: I want to go at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースに生きたい。

en: One who rides or travels in a vehicle, but who does not operate it and is not a member of the crew.
Somebody in a team who does not do their fair share of the work.
To ride as a passenger in a vehicle.

passenger.ety: From Old French passagier with intrusive n (see etymology of messenger).

ex.en: Why didn't they draw up a passenger list?
ex.ja: 彼らはなぜ乗客名簿を作らなかったのだろう。

ex.en: The bag I left on the passenger seat is missing!
ex.ja: 助手席に置いていた鞄がない！

ex.en: All the passengers were killed in the crash.
ex.ja: その墜落事故で乗客は全員死亡した。

en: An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle.
The bullpen.
To enclose in a pen.

pen.ety:
From Middle English pen, penne (“enclosure for animals”), from Old English penn (“enclosure, fold, pen”), from Proto-Germanic *pennō, *pannijō (“pin, bolt, nail, tack”), from Proto-Indo-European *bend- (“pointed peg, nail, edge”). Related to pin.
Sense “prison” originally figurative extension to “enclosure for persons” (1845), later influenced by penitentiary (“prison”), being analyzed as an abbreviation (1884).

ex.en: Please pick up the pen from the floor.
ex.ja: 床からペンを拾って下さい。

ex.en: To tell the truth, I've lost your pen.
ex.ja: 実を言うと、あなたのペンをなくしてしまったのです。

ex.en: Which is longer, this pen or that one?
ex.ja: このペンとあのペンではどちらが長いですか。

en: An honorary title of the Roman Catholic bishop of Rome as father and head of his church, a sovereign of the Vatican city state.
Any similarly absolute and 'infallible' authority.
To act as or like a pope.
To convert to Roman Catholicism.

pope.ety: From Middle English pope, popa, from Old English pāpa, from Vulgar Latin papa (title for priests and bishops, esp. and by 8th c. only the bishop of Rome), from early Medieval Greek παπᾶς (papâs, title for priests and bishops, especially by 3rd c. the bishop of Alexandria), from late Ancient Greek πάπας (pápas, title for priests and bishops, in the sense of spiritual father), from πάππας (páppas, “papa, daddy”).

ex.en: We have a Pope.
ex.ja: われらは教皇を得た。

ex.en: The pope appeared in his red robe.
ex.ja: 法王は赤い法衣をまとって現れた。

en: A control or occupancy of something for which one does not necessarily have private property rights.
Something that is owned.

possession.ety: From Latin possessiō, possessiōnis. Equivalent to possess + -ion.

ex.en: I have never had more than $500 in my possession.
ex.ja: 私は５００ドル以上を持ち歩いたことがありません。

ex.en: He is in possession of this land.
ex.ja: 彼はこの土地を所有している。

ex.en: All his possessions are contained in that box.
ex.ja: 彼の所持品は全部あの箱に入っている。

en: Very swift or quick.
Steep, changing altitude quickly. (of a slope)
A rough section of a river or stream which is difficult to navigate due to the swift and turbulent motion of the water.

ex.en: There was a rapid decline in stock prices.
ex.ja: 株価の急激な下落があった。

ex.en: The rapid growth of the city surprised us.
ex.ja: その都市の急速な発展に私たちは驚いた。

ex.en: There is a rapid increase in world population.
ex.ja: 世界の人口は急激に増加している。

en: The ordinal form of the number six.
The person or thing in the sixth position.
One of six equal parts of a whole.

sixth.ety: From earlier sixt, from Middle English sixte, from Old English siexta, from Proto-Germanic *sehstô. By surface analysis, six + -th (ordinal suffix).

ex.en: June is the sixth month of the year.
ex.ja: 「６月」は１年の中で６回目の月にあたります。

ex.en: She knew it by a sixth sense.
ex.ja: 彼女は第六感でそれが分かった。

ex.en: The office has been transferred up to the sixth floor.
ex.ja: 事務所は６階に移った。

en: To rotate, revolve, gyrate (usually quickly); to partially or completely rotate to face another direction.
To enter, or remain in, a spin (abnormal stalled flight mode).
Circular motion, usually rapid.
A state of confusion or disorientation.

spin.ety:
From Middle English spinnen, from Old English spinnan, from Proto-Germanic *spinnaną, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)penh₁-.
Cognates
Cognate with Dutch, German spinnen (“to spin”), Luxembourgish spannen (“to spin”), Yiddish שפּינען (shpinen, “spin”), Danish spinde (“to spin”), Faroese, Icelandic and Swedish spinna (“to spin”), Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk spinne (“to spin”), Gothic 𐍃𐍀𐌹𐌽𐌽𐌰𐌽 (spinnan, “to spin”).

ex.en: I'm so busy it makes my head spin.
ex.ja: 目が回るほど忙しいよ。

ex.en: After dinner, we took a spin around town in my car.
ex.ja: 食後、私の車で町を一走りした。

ex.en: My head is spinning because of the heat.
ex.ja: 暑さで頭が回らない。

en: The cardinal number occurring after twenty-nine and before thirty-one, represented in Arabic numerals as 30.
A commercial lasting 30 seconds.

thirty.ety: From Middle English thirty, metathetic alternant of thritty, from Old English þrītiġ, þrittiġ (“thirty”), from Proto-Germanic *þrīz tigiwiz (“thirty”, literally “three tens”), equivalent to three + -ty. ex.ja: トムは、30分ほど待ち続けている。

ex.ja: 彼女は３０歳の時に自殺した。

ex.en: She has been waiting for him thirty minutes.
ex.ja: 彼女は３０分彼を待っています。

en: Well-grounded or justifiable, pertinent.
Acceptable, proper or correct; in accordance with the rules.

ex.en: The ticket is valid for a week.
ex.ja: その切符は一週間有効です。

ex.en: This is a valid point of view.
ex.ja: これは十分根拠のある視点だ。

ex.en: This ticket is valid for three months.
ex.ja: この列車乗車券は３カ月有効だ。

en: Relating to or characteristic of life.
Necessary to the continuation of life; being the seat of life; being that on which life depends.

vital.ety: From Middle English vital, from Old French vital, from Latin vītālis (“of life, life-giving”), from vīta (“life”), from vīvō (“to live”). Doublet of jiva and quick.

ex.en: Public opinion plays a vital role in politics.
ex.ja: 世論は政治の領域で重要な役割を演ずる。

ex.en: Water is a natural resource of vital importance.
ex.ja: 水は極めて重要な天然資源の１つだ。

ex.en: In fact sleep is vital to us.
ex.ja: 実際、睡眠は人間にはどうしても欠かせない。

ex.ja: 混浴を楽しみながら会話に花をさかせました。

ex.en: Whilst on my way to school, I happened to catch sight of my uncle.
ex.ja: 学校に行く途中で、叔父さんを見掛けたんだ。

ex.ja: 彼は農業大学へ行きました。

ex.ja: 農業はその国の経済のもとである。

ex.ja: バイオテクノロジーは農業に革命をもたらすだろう。

en: To adduce (something) as a reason, excuse, support etc.
To make a claim as justification or proof; to make an assertion without proof.

ex.ja: その男がその殺人を犯したと言われている。

ex.ja: 彼は宝石を盗んだといわれている。

ex.ja: この車って、レギュラー？ハイオク？

ex.en: How much is the premium?
ex.ja: 保険料は幾らですか。

ex.en: I got a premium for subscribing to the magazine.
ex.ja: その雑誌の購読予約をして景品をもらった。

en: To speak or behave so as to give a false or simulated appearance.
To engage in make-believe.
Not really what it is represented as being; imaginary, feigned.
The act of engaging in pretend play.

pretend.ety:

From Anglo-Norman pretendre, Middle French pretendre (French prétendre (“to claim, demand”)), from Latin praetendere (“to put forward, hold out, pretend”), from prae- (“pre-”) + tendō (“stretch”); see tend.

ex.en: Tom, you're pretending to be asleep, aren't you?
ex.ja: トム、寝たふりしてるでしょ。

ex.en: The reason is they immediately pretend to know.
ex.ja: すぐ知ったかぶりをするんだから。

ex.en: Let's pretend that what happened today didn't happen.
ex.ja: 今日のことはなかったことにしよう。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ tend（伸ばす）。前に差し出して見せる →「ふりをする」。

en: A religious clergyman (clergywoman, clergyperson) who is trained to perform services or sacrifices at a church or temple.
A blunt tool, used for quickly stunning and killing fish.
To ordain as a priest.

priest.ety:
From Middle English prest, preest, from Old English prēost (“priest”), from Late Latin presbyter, from Ancient Greek πρεσβύτερος (presbúteros), from πρέσβυς (présbus, “elder, older”). Reinforced in Middle English by Old French prestre, also from Latin presbyter. Doublet of presbyter and prester.
* The Tyndale Bible uses native English elder instead.

ex.en: The priest made the sign of the cross.
ex.ja: 牧師は十字架を作った。

ex.en: According to one legend, it gets its name from a priest.
ex.ja: ある伝説によればそれはある聖職者の名からきている。

ex.en: The priest tried to improve the people's morals.
ex.ja: 祭司は人々を道徳的に高めようとした。

en: Standing out, or projecting; jutting; protuberant.
Likely to attract attention from its size or position; conspicuous.
Any of various moths having a conspicuous projection on the inner margin of the wings.
In Nazi concentration camps, an inmate entrusted with minor supervisory duties and rewarded with perquisites.

prominent.ety: From obsolete French prominent (compare proéminent), from Latin prōminēns, present active participle of prōmineō (“jut out, to project”), from prō (“before, forward”) + mineō (in compounds, “jut, project”).

ex.en: He occupies a prominent position in the firm.
ex.ja: 彼は会社で重要な地位を占めている。

ex.en: His white house is the most prominent one on the street.
ex.ja: 彼の真っ白な家はそのとおりで最も目立つ家だ。

ex.en: The prominent psychologist resembles my uncle in appearance.
ex.ja: その著名な心理学者は、見た目が私の叔父に似ている。

en: Of or pertaining to the root of a plant.
Of or pertaining to the root of a word.
A root (of a number or quantity).
In logographic writing systems such as the Chinese writing system, the portion of a character (if any) that provides an indication of its…

radical.ety:
PIE word
 *wréh₂ds
Inherited from Middle English radical, from Latin rādīcālis (“of or pertaining to the root, having roots, radical”). Compare grassroots.

ex.en: You'd better leave off such a radical idea.
ex.ja: そのような過激な考えはやめるべきだ。

ex.en: The government watched the activities of radical groups carefully.
ex.ja: 政府は過激派グループの活動を注意深く監視した。

ex.en: She has a very radical opinion about the problem.
ex.ja: 彼女はその問題についてとても過激な意見を持っている。

en: Of or pertaining to a place of personal residence or to a location for such places.
Used as a residence or by residents.
A trip during which people temporarily live together.

ex.en: This residential area is comfortable to live in.
ex.ja: この住宅地域は住み心地がよい。

ex.en: Tom and Mary live in a quiet residential neighborhood.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは閑静な住宅街に住んでいる。

ex.en: A factory is not suitable for a residential district.
ex.ja: 工場は住宅地域にはふさわしくない。

en: Something of value given in return for an act.
A prize promised for a certain deed or catch
To give a reward to or for.
To be a recompense for.

reward.ety:
From Middle English reward, rewarde, from Old French reward (“reward”) (compare Old French regard, whence modern French regard, and also English regard through Middle French), from rewarder (“to reward”) (compare Old French reguarder), from re- + warder (“to guard, keep”) (compare Old French guarder); the Anglo-Norman forms are derived from Old Northern French variants of Old French, ultimately of Germanic (Frankish) origin. Compare regard, warden, guard. See more below.
Mostly displaced Old English mēd, whence Modern English meed. Displaced Old English lēan and edlēan.

ex.en: He was too proud to accept any reward.
ex.ja: 報酬を受け取るのを彼のプライドが許さなかった。

ex.en: He wasn't given any reward for his service.
ex.ja: 彼は労働の報酬を何も貰わなかった。

ex.en: Not everyone is properly rewarded for his efforts.
ex.ja: 誰もが努力にふさわしい報酬を受けているわけではない。

en: A moon or other smaller body orbiting a larger one.
A man-made apparatus designed to be placed in orbit around a celestial body, generally to relay information, data, etc. to Earth.
To transmit by satellite.
To orbit, like a satellite

satellite.ety: From Middle French satellite, from Latin satelles (“attendant”). Ultimately perhaps of Etruscan origin.

ex.en: The moon is a satellite of the earth.
ex.ja: 月は地球の衛星である。

ex.en: The satellite is in orbit around the moon.
ex.ja: 衛星は月の周りの軌道に乗っている。

ex.en: Earth has one naturally occurring satellite, the Moon.
ex.ja: 地球は自然に発生した衛星を一つ有する。それは月だ。

en: To cause (something) to move rapidly in opposite directions alternatingly.
To move (one's head) from side to side, especially to indicate refusal, reluctance, or disapproval.
The act of shaking or being shaken; tremulous or back-and-forth motion.
A twitch, a spasm, a tremor.

shake.ety:

From Middle English schaken, from Old English sċeacan, sċacan (“to shake”), from Proto-West Germanic *skakan, from Proto-Germanic *skakaną (“to shake, swing, escape”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)keg-, *(s)kek- (“to jump, move”).
Cognate with Scots schake, schack (“to shake”), West Frisian schaekje (“to shake”), Dutch schaken (“to elope, make clean, shake”), Low German schaken (“to move, shift, push, shake”) and schacken (“to shake, shock”),

ex.en: Did you feel the earth shake just now?
ex.ja: 今し方地面がゆれたのを感じましたか。

ex.en: Did you feel the earth shake last night?
ex.ja: 昨夜、地震を感じましたか。

ex.en: Our eyes should meet when we shake hands.
ex.ja: 握手をする時には、視線を合わすべきだ。

en: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
Land, usually near a port.
Not followed by up: to provide (something) with support.
Usually followed by up: to reinforce (something at risk of failure).

shore.ety:
From Middle English schore, from Old English *sċora (attested as sċor- in placenames), from Proto-Germanic *skurô (“rugged rock, cliff, high rocky shore”). Possibly related to Old English sċieran (“to cut”), which survives today as English shear.
Cognate with Middle Dutch scorre (“land washed by the sea”), Middle Low German schor (“shore, coast, headland”), Middle High German schorre ("rocky crag, high rocky shore"; > German Schorre, Schorren (“towering rock, crag”)), and Limburgish sjaor (“riverbank”). Maybe connected with Norwegian Bokmål skjær.

ex.en: We walked along the shore of the lake.
ex.ja: 私たちは湖の岸に沿って歩いた。

ex.en: I found a beautiful shell on the shore.
ex.ja: 私は岸辺で美しい貝殻を見つけた。

ex.en: The ship stopped a little way off the shore.
ex.ja: その船は海岸を少し離れて停滞していた。

en: Having a substance; actually existing.
Not imaginary; real; actual; true; veritable.
Anything having substance; an essential part.

substantial.ety: From Middle English substancial, substantiall, from Old French substanciel, substantiel and its etymon Latin substantiālis.

ex.en: It will require substantial time and financial resources.
ex.ja: それにはかなりの時間と費用がかかります。

ex.en: Thanks to the opportunity, we were able to avoid substantial effort.
ex.ja: この機会のおかげで私たちは大いに手間暇が省けた。

ex.en: He made a substantial contribution to economics.
ex.ja: 彼は経済学に相当な貢献をした。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ stan（立つ）+ tial。下にしっかり立っているもの（substance 実体）の →「かなりの・実質的な」。

en: The act of transmitting, e.g. data (signals) or electric power.
The fact of being transmitted.

transmission.ety: Borrowed from Latin transmissionem (accusative of transmissio), from transmittere.

ex.en: 4-speed automatic transmission is available as an option.
ex.ja: オプションとして４速自動変速機も選べる。

ex.en: There might have been an error during transmission.
ex.ja: 受信異常があったのだと思います。

ex.en: Can you drive a car with manual transmission?
ex.ja: マニュアルシフトで運転できますか。

note.ja: trans（向こうへ）+ miss（送る）+ ion。向こうへ送ること →「伝達・送信・変速装置」。

en: A machine or other device designed to catch (and sometimes kill) animals, either by holding them in a container, or by catching hold of p…
A trick or arrangement designed to catch someone in a more general sense; a snare.
To physically capture, to catch in a trap or traps, or something like a trap.
To ensnare; to take by stratagem; to entrap.

trap.ety:
From Middle English trappe, from Old English træppe, treppe (“trap, snare”) (also in betræppan (“to trap”)) from Proto-West Germanic *trappjā (“trap, snare”), from Proto-West Germanic *trappjan (“to step”), from Proto-Germanic *trapjaną (“to tread, stamp”), from Proto-Indo-European *drebʰ- (“to step, trip, trample”).
Cognate with Dutch trap (“step, stair”), German Low German Trapp (“step, stair”). Akin also to West Frisian traap (“stepping, treading, stairway”), German Treppe (“step, stair”), Old English træppan (“to step, tread”). Connection to "step" is "that upon which one steps". French tr

ex.en: She fell into a trap in her turn.
ex.ja: 彼女は今度は自分が罠にはまった。

ex.en: Many workers were trapped in the coal mine.
ex.ja: 炭鉱の内部に多くの労働者が閉じ込められた。

ex.en: It looks like we fell into a trap.
ex.ja: どうやら俺たちは罠に嵌まったようだ。
